lines.rookie: The real piece was in Valli's box room. It has the owl and the Y-shaped crack. Pia and Sofia agreed: the market is closed on Sunday. So Valli's story was not true. Step by step, the evidence showed his plan. Then the pass he dropped made him tell the truth. He did not want to lose his money.
lines.junior: The real piece was hidden in Valli's box room; it has the owl and the Y-shaped crack. Pia and Sofia agreed that the market is closed on Sunday, so Valli's story was not true. Step by step, the evidence revealed his plan. Then the pass he had dropped made him tell the truth. He did not want to lose his money.
lines.master: The real piece had been hidden in Valli's box room, marked by the owl and the Y-shaped crack. Pia and Sofia agreed that the market is closed on Sunday, so Valli's story fell apart. Step by step, the evidence laid bare his plan, and the pass he had dropped finally forced the truth out of him. He did not want to lose his money.

lines.master: Then, ever so slowly, he sinks into his chair.

lines.rookie: Signor Valli says:
lines.junior: Signor Valli says:
lines.master: Signor Valli admits:

lines.rookie:
"All right. There is no Leo.
That pass is mine. I dropped it on Thursday night.
I saw the library on the new piece, before the show.
If people saw it, the city would stop my car park.
I paid for the land. I paid for the machines.
I did not want to lose my . . . . ."
lines.junior:
"All right. There is no Leo.
That pass is mine. I dropped it on Thursday night.
Before the show, I saw the library on the new piece.
If people saw it, the city would stop my car park.

lines.master:
"Very well. There is no Leo.
That pass is mine. I dropped it on Thursday night.
Before the show, I noticed the library carved on the new piece.
If people saw it, the city would stop my car park.
I had paid for the land, and for every machine on the site.
I could not bear to lose my . . . . ."

lines.rookie: What did Signor Valli not want to lose? Spell it.
lines.junior: What did Signor Valli not want to lose? Spell the word.
lines.master: What did Signor Valli not want to lose? Spell it out.

lines.rookie: He paid for the land and the machines. What do you pay with?
lines.junior: He had paid for the land and the machines. What do people pay with?
lines.master: Think about what he spent on the land and the machines.

lines.rookie: It is in your purse or your piggy bank.
lines.junior: You keep it in your purse or your piggy bank.
lines.master: It jingles in a piggy bank and folds into a purse.

lines.rookie: Signor Valli told the truth at last.
lines.junior: Signor Valli has told the truth at last.
lines.master: At long last, Signor Valli has told the truth.

lines.rookie: The inspector closes her notebook. "The work stops. Now."
lines.junior: The inspector closes her notebook. "The work stops. Right now."
lines.master: The inspector snaps her notebook shut. "The work stops. Now."

lines.rookie: There will be no concrete tomorrow.
lines.junior: No concrete will be poured tomorrow.
lines.master: Tomorrow, not a drop of concrete will be poured.

lines.rookie: Livia holds the real piece like a baby bird.
lines.junior: Livia holds the real piece as gently as a baby bird.
lines.master: Livia cradles the real piece as tenderly as a baby bird.

lines.rookie: All five tiles fit. What do you pay with?
lines.junior: All five tiles fit. What do people pay with?
lines.master: Every tile is in place. Now think about what people pay with.

lines.rookie: Show him the proof
lines.junior: Show him the proof
lines.master: Show him the proof

lines.rookie: Which thing in your Notebook did Signor Valli drop on Thursday night?
lines.junior: What in your Notebook did Signor Valli drop on Thursday night?
lines.master: Which item in your Notebook did Signor Valli let fall on Thursday night?

lines.rookie: Find the museum pass from Pia's cash box.
lines.junior: Look for the museum pass from Pia's cash box.
lines.master: Look for the museum pass that turned up in Pia's cash box.

lines.rookie: THE LAST WORD
lines.junior: THE LAST WORD
lines.master: THE LAST WORD

lines.rookie: I wanted my car park. That is all.
lines.junior: I just wanted my car park. That's all.
lines.master: All I wanted was my car park. Nothing more.

lines.rookie: You dropped this pass on Thursday night.
lines.junior: You dropped this pass on Thursday night.
lines.master: This pass fell from your pocket on Thursday night.

lines.rookie: Livia, you were right. I am sorry I did not listen.
lines.junior: Livia, you were right. I'm sorry I didn't listen to you.
lines.master: Livia, you were right all along. I'm sorry I didn't listen.

lines.rookie: Now we can open the owl square.
lines.junior: Now we can finally open the owl square.
lines.master: At last, the owl square can be opened.

lines.rookie: Under the fence, the old library is waiting.
lines.junior: Under the fence, the old library is still waiting.
lines.master: Beneath the fence, the old library lies waiting.
